# Onboarding acceptance references

Expected log fields, wire fields, labels, rotation and privacy rules come from the
product requirements. Clock values and sensitive identity strings in the tests are
injected inputs, not values generated by the application.

`contracts.json` publishes entry-point and data spellings. It contains no test logic.
The feedback payload library is shared by the form and its preview. Its transport is
injected; the tests never use a network service. The native payload probe evaluates the
production JavaScript in Qt, with fixed metadata and identity inputs.

The standalone log probe compiles the production `run_log.cpp` unchanged. It uses Qt's
installed message handler, a real QML engine, actual files, an injected clock and abrupt
process exit. The standalone target discards unused SDK-dependent host metadata
providers; the Qt-host actor checks the actual header provider separately. Placeholder
build metadata in this standalone target is unused, not an app-header oracle.

Build the native probes before timing or running acceptance nodes, from the pinned app
environment:

```
python tests/fixtures/onboarding/build_native.py log_probe
python tests/fixtures/onboarding/build_native.py payload_probe
```

Builds are prerequisites, as the production Qt test host is. Their compile time is not
a per-node test duration. A missing production helper is a feature red; a missing probe
or Qt environment is a prerequisite failure. No successful runtime bank may be inferred
from either failure.

The Qt actors instantiate production `Main` windows and click the real controls. The
URL probe intercepts HTTP/HTTPS dispatch without starting a browser or making requests.
The tutorial controls in `contracts.json` describe written-step navigation and project
isolation, not the later emulated player. Interface-tour callouts remain a separate gate.

`preview_gui_capture.txt` is the independent preview consumer, retained byte-for-byte
with source/blob attribution in `contracts.json`. It validates actual capture artifacts,
including hashes, sidebar coverage and scientific state. Generate the prerequisite by
running the normal native launcher through:

```
python tests/fixtures/onboarding/capture_bundle.py
```

The default bundle is `build/onboarding-capture`; override it with
`EDI_ONBOARDING_CAPTURE_BUNDLE`. The compatibility gate also binds the bundle to the
actual `EDI_DOCS_APP` executable (default `build/app/app/edi_app`). Generating captures
and compiling native probes happen outside pytest node timing. Capture generation is
pending until the source-matched native host exists; a saved arbitrary bundle is not a
substitute for the producer run.

`EDI_ONBOARDING_SOURCE_ROOT` permits replay against an archived pre-feature tree without
changing the shared checkout. Every claimed baseline replay names its archived commit.
Runtime proofs require source-matched native probes and the real Qt host; a cached
artifact without its identity checks cannot establish a current-head result.

`privacy_representations.json` supplies independently authored account/path spellings
and the accidental copy/paste or serialization route for each. Tests cover message text
with attachments off, nested metadata objects and arrays, and current/crash log text.
The payload probe parses JSON into actual JavaScript objects: Qt's wrapped QVariant
sequences are not a faithful stand-in for application arrays.

Log startup ownership is observed with two real processes and IPC barriers, an injected
clock and private app-data folders. A separate lock owner pauses before creating its log
to make the filename-reservation collision deterministic. Neither case sleeps or sends
traffic to an external endpoint.

Tutorial storage ownership uses the existing source-qualified transaction observer:

```
python -m tests.fixtures.project_transactions.build --root . --native build/app --output build/tutorial-transactions
```

`EDI_TRANSACTION_RECEIPT` can select its receipt. This observer links the real Qt Session
and installed SDK, and holds only the browser storage callbacks. Folder/archive/example,
upload, stored-place and recovery cases retain actual project objects and backing files.
It observes browser Session transactions; it is not a packed WebAssembly UI receipt.
The separate Qt actor drives Home reentry, pending Text edits, Stop/Keep/Discard and quit
through production controls. Build preparation belongs outside pytest node timing.

The navigation actor starts all three written tutorials through Home. Its lesson
state setup uses public model edits; Next, Back, Stop and Finish always receive
mouse input. A populated project exposes the Interface tour's workflow targets.
Placement is measured in scene coordinates against the real named control, never
against the production outline or locator's own answer. "Next to" allows two
narration text heights. The visible pointer is named `tutorial.pointer`; its own
rendered image must taper from the callout toward the target. This is an observation
name, not a replacement drawing or a reported direction flag.

The native observation helper can install a deterministic Qt animation driver.
A QML Timer sentinel proves delivered elapsed time before the no-auto-advance
assertion. No wall-clock sleep is used. Popup button styling is compared with the
actual Tutorials popup's standard Close button. Home links remain a different
control: left-aligned icon links without button chrome or column headers.

What's new accepts `EDI_CHANGELOG_JSON`, an array of `{date, text}` entries, as
its injected changelog source. The fixture deliberately lists dates out of order.
`Preferences.whatsNewSeen` is the persisted last-seen date. The popup is named
`whatsNew`, its rendered dated rows `whatsNew.day.<ISO date>`, and its full-page
link `whatsNew.page`. Tests inspect painted text and scene order, click
Show all versions, verify the actual settings file, and recreate the application
window to check one-time startup behavior. Ordinary runs use the bundled source.

URL observation catches HTTP(S), resource, local, relative, mail, data and script
schemes. The actual About feedback hyperlink is clicked, including the inherited
label handler, so duplicate external dispatch cannot hide behind the in-app form.
Choice-popup actors inspect painted labels and click actual delegates for every
feedback kind and logging level; changing only currentIndex cannot satisfy them.

The repeated-Keep ownership accident starts the same tutorial again after keeping
and editing/importing into its predecessor. Blank projects are saved first, so an
empty unsaved path is never mistaken for a backing folder. Example extraction
folders are exercised without saving them elsewhere. All old paths and bytes are
compared through multiple generations on native and browser Session routes.

`simulation-structure.edi` is independently authored from the written lesson's
cubic LBCO state. After the initially empty Structure step, the actor imports it
through the public project API and checks each stated group, cell and site state
before clicking Next. This is precondition setup, not tutorial action playback.
